summary: Nine new articles in myseliasan's built-in user manual, in all four shipped languages (36 files), taking the control plane's manual from 6 articles to 15 per language. Fleet: Managing a node (details are control-plane labels that change nothing on the appliance; working on a node's own screens over the control channel so the browser never touches the node; the certificate and the quiet way a node leaves the fleet when auto-renew is off; releasing vs remotely wiping; why an unrecognized node holding a VALID certificate is worth looking at), The notification feed (unread as a work queue rather than a badge; why the event rows live here while the footage stays on the node that recorded it; how one noisy source ruins a feed), and Fleet rules (correlating events across different nodes; why the 'must NOT have happened' half is what lets a rule express innocence and stops a legitimate badge entry being reported as an intrusion; what window, grace delay and cooldown each answer). Map & sites: The fleet map (placing nodes, the marker legend, and the split between your data and the PMTiles basemap -- so a control plane with no basemap shows a degraded map rather than a broken one, and why downloading a region is exactly the wrong move on a site that is meant to have no egress) and Buildings and floor plans (buildings vs outdoor areas vs point assets, areas named the way staff say them, uploading a plan image without losing walls or camera pins, and why a camera has exactly one pin and cannot be placed twice -- two pins would mean the system believes a device is in two rooms and every location-based answer built on it would quietly be wrong). Reports: the four PDFs, period and site scoping, and an honest account of the one real limitation -- report text uses a built-in Latin-script font, so CJK and Arabic characters in user-entered names render blank, with the practical workaround. AI agent: The fleet digest (findings are computed by ordinary code and appear whether or not a language model is enabled -- the model writes narrative over them and can neither invent nor suppress one), Ask the fleet (the two grounding sources, source citations, single-node drill-down, and what the assistant will not do), and Setting up a language model (off / external endpoint / managed sidecar, air-gapped Import where provenance is recorded rather than enforced, and how every path degrades instead of failing). Twenty of the questions these articles answer are now golden retrieval tests, so the fleet agent can answer for the control plane it runs on instead of only for the node appliances.
compatibility: Backward compatible, additive only. Content only -- no code, config, schema or route changes; the articles are markdown compiled into the binary by the existing //go:embed and served by the manual endpoints that already exist. The fleet-rules article was renumbered from 120 to 140 so the Fleet section reads in order (adopt, manage, notifications, rules); the numeric prefix is stripped when deriving the slug, so its slug, every cross-link and every deep link are unchanged. Two new stable category ids are introduced for grouping (map, reports) alongside the existing getting-started and fleet. Anchors are identical across all four languages and every cross-link resolves, so the manual conformance suite (metadata, language parity, links, anchors) and the contextual-help drift guard both still pass. Binary grows by roughly 150 KB of markdown.
